_meta.scope: Evidence base for a 'historical savings' model of the Iberian exception (RDL 10/2022, mecanismo de ajuste) for a PVPC household. Only figures found in the cited sources; any derived number is flagged with derived=true and its formula.
_meta.mechanism_active_period: Legally 15/06/2022 - 31/12/2023; in practice the adjustment was paid only until ~26/02/2023 (MIBGAS below the reference price afterwards: BdE DO 2316 note 41; OCU: 0 since March 2023).

household_reference.note: The mechanism acts only on the energy term (€/kWh); the 4.6 kW power term is unaffected. Savings below are pre-tax energy-term figures unless stated.

mechanism_parameters.formula: Y (cuantía unitaria de ajuste, €/MWh eléctrico) = (PGN - PRGN) / 0.55, where PGN = MIBGAS PVB spot gas price for the delivery day and PRGN = reference gas price; Y = 0 if negative. Fossil plants (CCGT, coal, cogeneration) must bid P - Y and are paid Y afterwards.

cap_schedule.period: from 7th month, +5 €/MWh per month (planned to 70 €/MWh in month 12; average 48.8 €/MWh over the original 12 months)

cap_schedule.prgn_eur_mwh: 56.1 in April, +1.1 per month, 65 in December

mechanism_parameters.financing: (i) part of the France-Spain congestion income and (ii) a charge (the 'ajuste') on buyers benefiting from the measure. PVPC consumers paid it on 100% of their energy from 15/06/2022 (embedded in the 'coste de la energía'); free-market fixed-price contracts signed before 26/04/2022 were exempt until renewal.

share_of_demand_paying.value: Spain 55.5% of energy bought in June 2022, 69.4% in December 2022 (MIBEL 52.6% -> 63.4%)

totals_2022.extra: average 73.94 €/MWh of energy subject to the charge

totals_2022.what: Additional congestion rents used to finance it (2022)

net_saving_per_household_eur_year.unit: € per PVPC household with 3,500 kWh/yr, pre-tax energy term, for the period the mechanism was materially active (15/06/2022 - 31/12/2022, ~6.5 months; Jan-Feb 2023 negligible)
net_saving_per_household_eur_year.method: Primary: EsadeEcPol 209 € per PVPC consumer (15/06-31/12/2022), scaled from 8 kWh/day (2,920 kWh/yr) to 3,500 kWh/yr: 209 x 3500/2920 = 250 € (derived). Cross-check with government data: PVPC net saving 314 M€ / PVPC energy (713 M€ adjustment / 126.8 €/MWh day-weighted OCU adjustment = 5.62 TWh) = ~56 €/MWh net, i.e. ~57 € for 106 days, ~195 €/yr if annualised for 3,500 kWh (derived). Low end 0: OIES / Linares-Gómez (elastic counterfactual, possibly no saving). High end 455: NERA 70 €/month x 6.5 months (industry study, secondary source).

caveats: Counterfactual dependence: official figures (MITECO 5,106 M€) use a static counterfactual (observed price + Y in every hour). BdE calls it an approximation; OIES and El Periódico de la Energía argue it overstates savings because lower prices raised exports/demand (price falls by less than Y). OIES and Linares-Gómez allow for zero or negative net saving.

Net vs gross: PVPC consumers paid the adjustment on 100% of their energy. Government data for 15/06-28/09/2022: PVPC gross saving 1,027 M€, adjustment 713 M€, net 314 M€ (net = ~31% of gross). MITECO 15-30 June 2022: -47% gross, -14% net.

Who benefited: the direct saving went to PVPC/indexed customers (~10 M in 2022; ~8 M today). Free-market fixed-price customers paid the adjustment after renewing contracts, often with no visible benefit (NERA: +63-111 €/month; industry-commissioned). Distributional effect matters more today: Aelec says 3 of 4 consumers are on fixed price.

Exports subsidy: lower Iberian prices increased exports to France (Esade: +80%; Columbia: ~0.6 bn € transferred; NERA: 800 M€ France + 575 M€ Morocco). BdE counter-view: in ~70% of hours the FR-ES spread exceeded Y, so interconnection would likely have been saturated anyway.

Gas price dependence: savings scale with (gas price - cap)/0.55 and with the share of hours where gas is marginal. In Aug 2022 MIBGAS averaged 165.85 €/MWh and gas set the price in ~75% of hours (Aelec); in Sept-Oct 2026 MIBGAS is ~70-77 €/MWh and gas sets the price in <15% of hours (Aelec). Applying 2022 savings to 2026 would overstate the effect.

PVPC is now less exposed to spot: since the 2023 PVPC reform the energy component is partly indexed to futures (45% spot / 55% futures when fully phased in, per La Vanguardia 13/06/2023), so a spot-price reduction passes through less than in 2022.
Higher gas use and emissions: the mechanism increased CCGT generation (Columbia: Spanish gas for power +52.7% in 2022; El Nacional/NERA: ~1 Mt CO2, +2.5%).

Unit/period consistency: Esade's 209 € is per average PVPC consumer (assumed 8 kWh/day) for 15/06-31/12/2022, not a calendar year. Monthly OMIE pool for June 2022 includes 1-14 June (pre-mechanism). OCU adjustment values are monthly profile averages (€/kWh) for PVPC/indexed customers.

Some 2026 press pieces contain errors about the 2022 mechanism (e.g. Cinco Días 23/09/2026 says a '50 €/MWh' cap 'a partir de 2024'; the real cap was 40 €/MWh from 15/06/2022). Use primary sources (BOE RDL 10/2022, EC decision) for parameters.
EU legal constraint: in 2022 the EC authorised it as state aid under art. 107(3)(b) TFEU because of Iberia's limited interconnection; reapplying it would require new EC approval.
